name: 拨珠坡
Abacus Slope
before: 野地里一道缓坡，漂客们排着队换东西，队头坐着个十来岁的丫头，怀里抱着一架比她还宽的大算盘，谁换了什么、换了多少，她噼里啪啦一拨，就记进一本破账里。一队亡骑嫌算珠吵，三番五次来抢她的算盘，她抱着算盘满坡跑，账本咬在嘴里。

On a gentle slope castaways queue to barter, and at the head of the line sits a girl of ten or so with an abacus wider than she is. Whoever trades what, however much, she clacks it out on the beads and writes it into a tattered ledger. A troop of dead riders hates the clatter and keeps coming to snatch the abacus, and she runs all over the slope hugging it, the ledger clamped in her teeth.
after: 亡骑跑了，丫头吐出账本，自报名叫珠珠，是在归墟生的。算盘框上刻着「千里号·丝路·账房备用」，是「驼客」留给她的。驼客是她对丝路那帮人的叫法：「他们算账可凶了。」她翻开账本最后几页：她在记千里号的人，记一个，画一个圈，还差得远。

The riders flee and the girl spits out her ledger. Her name is Zhuzhu and she was born in the Ruins. Carved on the abacus frame is 'Qianli. Silk Road. Bookkeeper's spare', left to her by the 'camel folk', which is what she calls the Silk Road people. 'They were fierce at sums.' She turns to the last pages of the ledger: she is recording the Qianli's people, a circle for each one, and she still has a long way to go.

name: 老鼎灶
Old Ding's Stove
before: 大路边一座石砌的大灶，灶口能钻进一个人，灶上坐着一口大锅，锅里能洗澡。灶冷了好些年，一队亡弓却天天围着它坐，弓搁在膝上，像在等开饭。漂客们想借锅煮鱼，一靠近就挨箭，只好远远看着那口锅咽口水。

Beside the main road stands a great stone stove with a fire mouth a man could crawl into and a cauldron on top big enough to bathe in. It has been cold for years, yet a squad of dead archers sits around it every day, bows across their knees, as if waiting for dinner. The castaways would love to boil fish in it, but anyone who comes near gets shot, so they just gaze at the pot from a distance and swallow.
after: 亡弓散了，漂客们生了火，鱼汤的香味飘出半里。珠珠在账上画了一个圈：「老鼎，大厨，胖。」灶台上刻着他的规矩：「锅按三百人煮，多出来的一碗，给晚到的。」漂客们说，那几年这口锅里天天剩一碗，到第二天倒了，再剩一碗。

The archers scatter, the castaways light a fire, and the smell of fish soup carries half a li. Zhuzhu draws a circle in her ledger: 'Old Ding. Head cook. Fat.' His rule is carved on the stove: 'Cook for three hundred. The extra bowl is for whoever comes late.' In those years, the castaways say, there was a bowl left over in this pot every day. Next morning it was poured away, and another bowl was left.

name: 接生棚
Midwife's Shelter
before: 野地里一座大草棚，棚檐下挂着一排晒干的草药，门口的石臼还沾着药渣。三路守墟人把棚子团团围住，亡兵堵门，亡弓上了棚顶，亡骑绕着外圈。棚里躺着一个快临盆的漂客媳妇，接生婆被拦在外头，急得拍大腿：「再拖下去，两条命！」

A large grass shelter stands in the open, dried herbs hanging along its eaves and a stone mortar at the door still crusted with medicine. Ruin-keepers in three columns surround it: soldiers block the door, archers on the roof, riders circling outside. Inside lies a castaway woman about to give birth, and the midwife, kept outside, slaps her thighs in despair. 'Any longer and it's two lives!'
after: 守墟人退了，天黑前棚里传出一声响亮的啼哭。接生婆擦着手说，她这手艺是千里号上的柳娘子教的，那几年归墟生的孩子，个个是柳娘子接的。珠珠红着脸画了个圈：「柳医，女的，手凉。」她自己就是柳娘子接生的。

The keepers withdraw and before nightfall a loud wail rings out from the shelter. Wiping her hands, the midwife says she learned her craft from Doctor Liu, the woman on the Qianli. Every child born in the Ruins in those years was delivered by Doctor Liu. Zhuzhu blushes as she draws a circle: 'Doctor Liu. A woman. Cold hands.' She was one of those babies herself.

name: 断弦亭
Broken String Pavilion
before: 野地里一座竹亭，亭柱上挂着一把琵琶，弦全断了，只剩一根。漂客家的孩子常来这儿唱歌，唱的是一程水一程雾。一队亡骑嫌吵，拿枪杆挑断了琴弦，又拿渔网把亭子罩了起来。打到最后，一个亡骑被自己的网缠住了，连人带马倒在泥里，挣不出来。

A bamboo pavilion in the open, a pipa hanging from one of its posts, every string broken but one. The castaways' children come here to sing, the song about a stretch of water and a stretch of fog. A troop of dead riders, sick of the noise, snapped the strings with their spear butts and threw a fishing net over the whole pavilion. By the end of the fight one rider is tangled in his own net, horse and all, stuck in the mud.
after: 别的亡骑都退了，那一个还在网里挣。你们没补刀，割开网，把他和马拽了出来。他站起来，冲你们低了低那张没有五官的脸，牵着马走进了水里，枪头上挂着的一枚驼铃叮了一声。珠珠画了个圈：「弹琵琶的，姓什么不知道，歌是他教的。」

The other riders retreat, but that one is still thrashing in the net. You don't finish him. You cut the net and haul him and his horse free. He stands, dips that featureless face towards you, and leads his horse into the water, a camel bell on his spearhead giving one small chime. Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'The pipa player. Surname unknown. He taught us the song.'

name: 暗渠田
Hidden Channel Field
before: 野地里一片芋头田，地底下埋着一条暗渠，从山脚引水过来，每隔几十步有一口竖井。一队亡弓守在竖井边，往井里一筐筐地填沙，填满一口，田里的芋头叶就黄一片。种田的漂客说，这渠是驼客挖的，挖渠的人里有个姓周的，挖井挖得最快。

A taro field lies in the open with a hidden channel buried beneath it, bringing water from the foot of the hills, a shaft sunk every few dozen paces. A squad of dead archers stands by the shafts tipping in basket after basket of sand, and each time one fills, a patch of taro leaves yellows. The camel folk dug this channel, say the farmers, and among the diggers was a man named Zhou who sank shafts faster than anyone.
after: 亡弓被赶走，竖井一口口掏开，水又流了起来。最后一口井的井沿上刻着「老周」，旁边一行小字：「在王城挖了二百九十九口，到这儿挖第三百口。」坎儿井的手艺从沙漠一路带到了海边。珠珠画了个圈：「老周，挖井的，爱哼小调。」

The archers are driven off, the shafts dug out one by one, and the water runs again. On the curb of the last shaft is carved 'Old Zhou', and beside it in small characters: 'Dug two hundred and ninety-nine at the royal city. Digging the three hundredth here.' The craft of the desert's underground channels had come all the way to the sea. Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'Old Zhou. Well digger. Loved humming tunes.'

name: 三碗亭
Three Bowl Pavilion
before: 大路正中一座石亭，亭里一张石桌，桌面上嵌着三只碗：一只青瓷，一只粗陶，一只铜的。碗里各有一层干了的渍，一碗红，一碗褐，一碗白。一队亡弓守着石亭，谁想往碗里倒东西，就把谁的手射穿在桌上。

A stone pavilion stands squarely in the main road with a stone table inside and three bowls set into its top: one celadon, one coarse clay, one copper. Each holds a dried stain, one red, one brown, one white. A squad of dead archers guards the pavilion and will pin to the table the hand of anyone who tries to pour something in.
after: 亡弓退了。龚墨斗舔了舔指头，挨个尝过：红的是葡萄酒，褐的是茶，白的是盐，是海水干了。三路的人在这里会了面，各倒一碗，换着喝了。桌沿刻着一行字：「三路至。缺者三，候之一年。」珠珠说她听大人讲过那天，人人都哭了，哭完又笑，笑完接着等。

The archers withdraw. Gong Modou licks a fingertip and tastes each in turn: the red is grape wine, the brown is tea, the white is salt, dried seawater. The three roads met here, each poured a bowl, and they drank one another's. Carved on the table's edge is a line: 'The three roads have come. Three are missing. We wait one year.' Zhuzhu says she heard the grown-ups talk about that day: everyone cried, then laughed, then went on waiting.

name: 半船坞
Half-Built Slip
before: 海边一座小船坞，坞里架着半条小船，龙骨、肋骨都齐了，船板只钉了一边，像一条被剖开的鱼。一队亡兵占着船坞，把钉好的船板一块块撬下来扔进海里。看坞的漂客老汉说，造船的人走了好些年，这半条船他替人家看着，不能叫它烂了。

A small slipway on the coast cradles half a boat: keel and ribs complete, planking on one side only, like a fish split open. A squad of dead soldiers has taken the slip and is prising off the fitted planks one by one and throwing them into the sea. The old castaway who keeps the slip says the man who was building it left years ago. He has looked after the half-boat for him all this time. He can't let it rot.
after: 亡兵退了，船板捞回来大半。船头刻着两个字：「阿菱」。老汉说造船的是个姓郑的水手，想造条小船回泉州，造了一半，大伙要往东走了，他放下斧头跟着走了：「他说，回去的路有人走过了，往前的路还没有。」珠珠画了个圈，想了想又问：「阿菱是谁？」

The soldiers retreat and most of the planks are fished back out. Two characters are carved on the bow: 'A Ling'. The builder was a sailor named Zheng, the old man says, who wanted to build a little boat and sail back to Quanzhou. He was halfway done when everyone made ready to go east, and he put down his axe and went with them. 'He said somebody had already walked the road home. The road ahead, nobody had.' Zhuzhu draws a circle, thinks, then asks: 'Who's A Ling?'

name: 算学棚
Counting School
before: 野地里一座矮棚，棚里摆着几十只小板凳，墙上一块大石板，石板上写着算式。这是驼客给漂客家孩子开的算学，教打算盘。一队亡兵占了棚子，排排坐在小板凳上，板凳压塌了好几张，他们还坐着，一动不动，像一班学不会的笨学生。

A low shelter in the open with dozens of little stools and a great slate on the wall covered in sums. It is the arithmetic school the camel folk opened for the castaways' children, teaching the abacus. A squad of dead soldiers has taken it over and sits in rows on the little stools. Several stools have collapsed beneath them and still they sit, motionless, like a class too dim ever to learn.
after: 亡兵起身走了，珠珠第一个冲进去，摸着石板直掉眼泪：这是她的学堂。石板上还留着先生出的最后一道题：「三百减二百九十九，得几？」底下是孩子们的答案：「一」。先生拿红土把「一」圈了，旁边改了一行：「得一个后来的。」

The soldiers get up and leave, and Zhuzhu is first through the door, stroking the slate with tears running down: this was her school. The teacher's last question is still on it: 'Three hundred minus two hundred and ninety-nine makes what?' Beneath it the children's answer: 'One.' The teacher circled the 'one' in red clay and wrote beside it: 'Makes one who comes after.'

name: 剃头凳
Barber's Stool
before: 野地里一张高脚凳，凳边一只铜盆，盆沿挂着一条发黄的手巾。每天清早，一个亡弓过来，在凳子上坐下，仰起头，等着。没人给他剃，他就一直坐到天黑。今天来了一队，争着坐那张凳子，挤成一团，把来剃头的漂客全赶跑了。

A tall stool stands in the open with a brass basin beside it and a yellowed towel over the rim. Every morning one dead archer comes, sits on the stool, tips his head back and waits. Nobody shaves him, so he sits there till dark. Today a whole squad has come, jostling over the stool in a heap, and they have chased away every castaway who came for a shave.
after: 亡弓散了。漂客们说，凳子是千里号上的剃头匠刘一刀的，每月初一，他给二百多号人挨个剃一遍，连守墟人都爱凑过来坐一坐。「他也给它们剃，」一个老汉笑，「脸上没东西，他就拿刀背刮一刮，说精神。」珠珠画了个圈：「刘一刀，剃头的，话多。」

The archers scatter. The stool belonged to Liu One-Stroke, the Qianli's barber, the castaways say. On the first of every month he shaved two hundred-odd people one after another, and even the keepers liked to come and sit for a turn. 'He shaved them too,' an old man laughs. 'Nothing on their faces, so he'd scrape them with the back of the razor and say it freshened them up.' Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'Liu One-Stroke. Barber. Talked a lot.'

name: 葡萄屿
Vine Islet
before: 南屿背风的一面，石缝里爬满了葡萄藤，一串串紫得发黑。海岛上长葡萄，漂客们都说是个怪事。一队亡兵守在藤架底下，把熟了的葡萄一串串揪下来扔进海里，扔得满滩紫汁，就是不许人摘一颗。

On the lee side of the South Islet, grapevines creep through every crack in the rock, bunches so purple they are almost black. Grapes on a sea island: the castaways call it a wonder. A squad of dead soldiers guards the trellises, tearing off the ripe bunches one by one and hurling them into the sea until the beach runs purple, and they will not let anyone pick a single grape.
after: 亡兵退了，漂客们挎着篮子上了屿。藤是驼客从王城带来的，插枝裹在湿毡里，过了沙漠、过了雪山，一路没死。种藤的人叫葡萄张，他说过：「葡萄认人，谁种的，它就替谁记着年头。」珠珠尝了一颗，酸得眯眼，画了个圈：「葡萄张，种藤的，牙不好。」

The soldiers fall back and the castaways climb the islet with baskets. The camel folk brought the vines from the royal city, cuttings wrapped in wet felt, across desert and over snow mountains, and not one died on the way. The man who planted them was called Grape Zhang, and he used to say, 'A vine knows its planter. It keeps count of the years for him.' Zhuzhu tries one, screws up her eyes at the sourness, and draws a circle: 'Grape Zhang. Grows vines. Bad teeth.'

name: 丝帆湾
Silk Sail Cove
before: 海边一道小湾，湾里泊着十几条漂客的渔船，船上挂的帆一张张流光溢彩，是绸子做的，红的、青的、织着团花。一队亡骑冲进湾里，拿枪尖把帆一张张挑破，挑破的绸子挂在桅上，耷拉下来，像一面面褪了色的旗。

A small cove on the coast shelters a dozen castaway fishing boats, and their sails shimmer: they are made of silk, red and blue, woven with roundel patterns. A troop of dead riders charges into the cove and slashes the sails one by one with their spear points, the torn silk drooping from the masts like faded banners.
after: 亡骑退了，渔家把绸子收下来缝补。绸边上都印着驼队的记号：「丝路·第几驮」。那年一场大雨淋了丝路的货，绸子泡了盐水卖不出去，驼客就裁了给渔家做帆：「货是死的，帆是活的。」珠珠画了个圈：「裁帆的，女的，手快，脾气大。」

The riders retreat and the fishing families take down the silk to mend it. Every selvedge is stamped with the caravan's mark: 'Silk Road, load number such-and-such.' One year a great storm soaked the Silk Road's goods, the silk was ruined with salt and couldn't be sold, so the camel folk cut it up for the fishermen's sails. 'Goods just sit there. Sails go places.' Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'The one who cut the sails. A woman. Quick hands, quick temper.'

name: 三路沙盘
Three Roads Sand Table
before: 野地里一大片平地上，用沙子、石子和贝壳堆出了一幅天下：西北一片黄沙是大漠，西南一溜红土是茶山，南边一摊碎贝壳是海，三条石子路从三头弯弯绕绕，最后汇到一个地方。一队亡弓正在沙盘上踩来踩去，一脚下去，一座山就塌了。

On a broad flat stretch of open ground, the whole world has been laid out in sand, pebbles and shells: yellow sand in the north-west for the great desert, a strip of red earth in the south-west for the tea mountains, a spread of crushed shell in the south for the sea, and three pebble roads winding in from three directions to meet at one point. A squad of dead archers is tramping all over it; one step and a mountain collapses.
after: 亡弓退了，龚墨斗蹲下来把踩塌的山一座座扶起来。三条路汇合的地方插着一根小竹签，签上写「归墟」。可从归墟往东，还有第四条石子路，一直铺到沙盘边上，铺出去了，沙盘外头什么也没有。珠珠说，驼客天天来添这条路，添一点，量一量，摇摇头。

The archers withdraw and Gong Modou squats to stand the trampled mountains back up one by one. Where the three roads meet a little bamboo slip is planted, labelled 'the Ruins'. But from the Ruins a fourth pebble road runs on east, all the way to the edge of the table and off it, into nothing at all. The camel folk came every day to add to that road, Zhuzhu says. They'd add a little, measure it, and shake their heads.

name: 借名村
Borrowed Names Village
before: 野地里一座小村，村里二三十个孩子，见了你们就躲。一队亡骑这几天天天进村，在每户门口停一停，像在点名，点完了就走，走了明天又来。村里的大人把孩子锁在屋里，说守墟人是来「收名字」的。

A little village in the open with twenty or thirty children who hide as soon as they see you. For days a troop of dead riders has ridden in every day, pausing at each door as if calling a roll, then leaving, then coming back the next day. The grown-ups lock their children indoors and say the keepers have come to 'collect names'.
after: 亡骑被赶走，孩子们才敢出来，一个个报名字：小鼎、阿柳、琶琶、一刀、周周……全是千里号的人名。大人说那几年生的孩子，都拿千里号的人起名，那些人走的时候说：「名字留下，人就还在。」珠珠一个一个对着账本打勾，对到最后，抬头问：「我呢？我的名字是谁的？」

Once the riders are driven off the children dare come out and give their names one by one: Little Ding, A Liu, Pipa, One-Stroke, Zhou Zhou... every one a name from the Qianli. Children born in those years were all named after the Qianli's people, the adults say, and when those people left they said, 'Leave the names, and we're still here.' Zhuzhu ticks them off against her ledger one by one, and at the end she looks up. 'What about me? Whose name is mine?'

name: 守灯铺
Lamp Keeper's Shop
before: 海边一座矮石塔，塔顶一盏灯，塔下一间铺子，卖灯油、灯芯、火石。守灯的是个瘦高的老汉，夜夜点灯，给撞进礁圈的船指路。可这一个月一队亡骑天天在塔下转，见火就扑，灯点一回灭一回，铺子也不许开门，老汉坐在门槛上，捏着一截灯芯发呆。

A squat stone tower on the coast with a lamp on top and a shop below selling lamp oil, wicks and flints. The keeper is a tall, thin old man who lights the lamp every night to guide ships that blunder into the reef ring. But for a month a troop of dead riders has circled the tower daily, pouncing on any flame. Every time he lights the lamp it goes out again, and he isn't allowed to open the shop either. He sits on the doorstep turning a wick between his fingers.
after: 亡骑被赶走，灯又亮了，铺门也开了，老汉佩服你们，拿灯油、火石跟你们换货。他说千里号的人来时，他的灯油早用光了，是他们分了他一桶鲸油，叮嘱一句：「灯别灭，后头还有人。」「后头的人，」他看看你们桅上的灯笼，「原来是你们。」

The riders are driven away, the lamp burns again, the shop opens, and the old man, impressed, trades you lamp oil and flints for your goods. When the Qianli's people came, he says, his oil had long run out, and they gave him a barrel of whale oil with one instruction: 'Don't let the lamp go out. There are more coming.' He looks up at the lanterns on your masts. 'The ones coming after. So it was you.'

name: 醒酒坡
Sober-Up Slope
before: 野地里一面向阳的土坡，坡上埋着几百只酒坛，坛口封着泥，泥上按着手印。一队亡骑正拿枪尖一只只撬坛口，撬开了也不喝，倒在地上，满坡酒气，熏得坡下放羊的漂客直打晃，羊也醉倒了好几只，躺在草里蹬腿。

A sunny slope in the open has several hundred wine jars buried in it, their mouths sealed with clay and a handprint pressed into each seal. A troop of dead riders is prising them open with spear points, and having opened them, they don't drink, they pour them out. The whole slope reeks of wine, the castaways herding goats below are reeling, and several goats have passed out too, lying in the grass kicking their legs.
after: 亡骑被赶走，剩下的坛子又封了回去。坛上贴着签：葡萄酒、米酒、青稞酒，三路各有。放羊的说，这是那几年三路的人一起埋的，说好等缺的那几个都到了再开，「开坛那天，一醉三天」。坛子埋到今天，一只都没开过。珠珠在账上写：「酒，没喝。」

The riders are driven off and the surviving jars are sealed again. Each carries a label: grape wine, rice wine, highland barley wine, something from every road. The three roads buried them together in those years, says the goatherd, and agreed to open them once the missing ones arrived. 'The day we open them, three days drunk.' They have lain buried till today and not one has been opened. Zhuzhu writes in her ledger: 'Wine. Not drunk.'

name: 晒鲞场
Fish-Drying Flats
before: 海边一大片晒场，竹架上本该挂满剖开的鱼，如今被一伙落难海盗占了：他们的船撞在礁上沉了，上了岸，就抢渔家的晒场，晒好的鱼他们吃，没晒好的他们也吃。守场的是几个骑着抢来的瘦骡子的，骡子饿得啃竹架，架子塌了一排又一排。

A wide drying ground on the coast where the bamboo racks ought to be hung with split fish. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it: their ship struck the reef and sank, they came ashore, and they seized the fishing families' flats. They eat the dried fish, and the half-dried fish too. The guards ride scrawny stolen mules so hungry they gnaw the racks, which collapse row after row.
after: 海盗被赶下了场，竹架重新立起来，一排排鱼鲞又挂满了，海风不吹，太阳照样晒。渔家说，晒鲞的法子是千里号的老鼎教的：盐抹七分，晒三日，翻两回。珠珠在账上添了一笔，老鼎的圈旁边多了一条小鱼。

The pirates are driven off the flats, the racks go back up, and row after row of split fish hang there again. There is no sea breeze, but the sun dries them just the same. Old Ding from the Qianli taught them how, the fishing families say: rub in seven parts salt, dry for three days, turn twice. Zhuzhu adds a stroke in her ledger, a little fish beside Old Ding's circle.
first: 海盗的窝棚里抄出三百斤鱼鲞、半船舱的硬饼、两桶淡水、一口抢来的大铁锅，还有一箱他们一路抢来的金银首饰，到了归墟，没地方花，拿来压咸鱼。

In the pirates' shacks you seize three hundred jin of dried fish, half a hold of hard biscuit, two barrels of fresh water, a big stolen iron pot, and a chest of gold and silver jewellery looted along the way. With nowhere to spend it in the Ruins, they had been using it to weigh down the salt fish.
pass: 每次路过，渔家都往你们车上码一捆鱼鲞，按老鼎的法子晒的，再塞一小包盐：「路上自己会晒鱼，就饿不着。」

Each time you pass, the fishing families stack a bundle of dried fish on your carts, made Old Ding's way, and tuck in a little packet of salt besides. 'If you can dry your own fish on the road, you'll never go hungry.'

name: 无名坟
Nameless Mound
before: 野地里一个小土包，包前没立碑，插着一根竹竿，竿头挂着一只婴儿的银锁。珠珠一看见它就站住了。一队亡兵围着土包站成一圈，背朝外，像在守着什么，谁也不许走近。珠珠攥着算盘的手直发抖：「我娘说过，我是从这里捡回去的。」

A small earth mound in the open, no headstone in front of it, only a bamboo pole with a baby's silver lock hanging from the top. Zhuzhu stops dead when she sees it. A squad of dead soldiers stands in a ring around the mound, facing outward as if guarding something, and will let no one near. Zhuzhu's hands shake on her abacus. 'Mother told me she found me here.'
after: 亡兵退了。土包不是坟，是一座小小的地窖，窖里铺着干草，摆着一只摇篮，摇篮上刻着「千里号·木作」。银锁背面刻着两个字：「珠算」。珠珠的娘说了实话：那年一个驼客的媳妇在这里生了她，夫妻俩要往东走，路太远，就把孩子托给了漂客。「他们说，等回来，账算清了，再接她。」

The soldiers withdraw. The mound is not a grave but a tiny cellar, lined with dry straw, with a cradle in it carved 'Qianli. Carpentry'. Engraved on the back of the silver lock are two characters: 'Abacus Count'. Zhuzhu's mother tells the truth at last: that year a camel man's wife gave birth to her here. The couple were going east, the road was too long to carry a baby, so they left her with the castaways. 'They said they'd come back for her when the accounts were settled.'

name: 锚冢滩
Anchor Barrow Beach
before: 海滩上离水二三十步，一字排开埋着四只大铁锚，锚爪朝天，锚杆插进沙里，像四块墓碑。一队亡骑绕着铁锚来回地跑，跑一圈，拿枪杆敲一下锚爪，当的一声。漂客们说，他们敲了好些年，敲的次数都一样，一天四下。

Twenty or thirty paces above the waterline, four great iron anchors are planted in a row on the beach, flukes skyward, shanks driven into the sand like four headstones. A troop of dead riders gallops round and round them, striking a fluke with a spear butt on every lap, clang. They have been striking them for years, the castaways say, always the same number: four a day.
after: 亡骑散了。锚杆上铸着字：「千里·二」「千里·三」「千里·四」「千里·五」。小桨摸到每只锚环上都打着一个结，正是爷爷鲍老针的结法。龚墨斗皱起眉头：锚上了岸，船就不打算走了。可船呢？四条船，一条也没看见。

The riders scatter. Cast into the shanks are the words 'Qianli Two', 'Qianli Three', 'Qianli Four', 'Qianli Five'. Xiaojiang feels a knot tied on every anchor ring, tied the way his grandfather Bao Laozhen tied them. Gong Modou frowns. Bring your anchors ashore and you don't mean to sail again. But where are the ships? Four ships, and not one in sight.

name: 船肋桥
Ship Rib Bridge
before: 大路过一道干沟，沟上架着一座桥，桥拱是一根根弯木，一看就是船的肋骨，桥面是船板，还留着钉眼。一队亡兵守着桥，只许往西走，不许往东过。漂客挑着担子要过桥去东边换东西，被一枪杆拨回来，再上，再拨回来。

The main road crosses a dry gully on a bridge whose arches are curved timbers, plainly a ship's ribs, and whose deck is ship's planking still pocked with nail holes. A squad of dead soldiers guards it and lets people cross westward only, never east. A castaway with a carrying pole tries to cross east to trade and is flicked back with a spear shaft, tries again, and is flicked back again.
after: 亡兵退了，挑担的漂客过了桥。龚墨斗趴在桥底下看了半天：肋骨上烙着「千里·三」，可好几根上有一层焦黑，是火烧过的。他脸色不好看：「烧过的船，拆下来架桥？」漂客说，船是烧了的，他听人讲过，至于谁烧的，他就说不清了。

The soldiers fall back and the castaway crosses with his load. Gong Modou lies under the bridge studying it a long while: 'Qianli Three' is branded on the ribs, but several are scorched black. Fire has been at them. His face darkens. 'They burned a ship, then pulled it apart for a bridge?' The ship was burned, the castaway says, he has heard as much. Who burned it, he couldn't say.

name: 船头屋
Prow House
before: 北屿的崖下卡着一截船头，船头朝天，雕着一只张嘴的海兽，嘴里能钻进人。一个老阿婆住在海兽嘴里，养着一窝鸡。一队亡弓蹲在崖上，冲船头射箭，射得海兽一脸的箭，老阿婆在嘴里拿锅盖挡着，鸡飞了一崖。

A ship's prow is wedged beneath a cliff on the North Islet, pointing skyward, carved as a sea beast with gaping jaws big enough to crawl into. An old woman lives inside the beast's mouth with a brood of chickens. A squad of dead archers crouches on the clifftop shooting at the prow until the beast's face bristles with arrows, the old woman shielding herself inside with a pot lid while chickens flap all over the cliff.
after: 亡弓被赶走了。阿婆说这是「千里·四」的船头，那年她亲眼看见守墟人拿斧头把船劈开的，「船是它们劈的，一夜之间，四条船」。龚墨斗看了看船头断口：是锯的，不是劈的，锯口整整齐齐。阿婆一摆手：「我老了，眼神不好，可我听得见斧子响。」

The archers are driven off. This is the prow of Qianli Four, the old woman says. She saw with her own eyes the keepers hack the ship apart with axes. 'They split them, one night, all four ships.' Gong Modou looks at the break: it was sawn, not hacked, a neat clean cut. The old woman waves a hand. 'I'm old, my eyes are poor. But I heard axes.'

name: 指路桅
Signpost Mast
before: 六条路交会的地方立着一根粗桅杆，高过所有的树，杆上钉着四块指路牌。一队亡兵围着桅杆站岗，谁走到跟前抬头看牌子，就被他们推着转三圈，转晕了，往哪条路走都不知道。路口已经坐了好几个转晕的漂客，扶着脑袋干呕。

Where six roads meet stands a thick mast taller than any tree, four signboards nailed to it. A squad of dead soldiers stands guard round it, and anyone who walks up and looks at the boards gets spun round three times until they're too dizzy to know which road to take. Several dizzy castaways already sit at the crossroads, clutching their heads and retching.
after: 亡兵散了。四块牌子分别写着：「泉州，一万二千里」「茶山，八千里」「王城，九千里」，第四块朝东，只写了一个字：「前」。没有里数。桅杆脚下系着一根绳，绳上一串结，小桨一个个摸过去：「是爷爷的结。他说，往东的路量不出来。」

The soldiers scatter. The four boards read 'Quanzhou, twelve thousand li', 'Tea Mountains, eight thousand li', 'Royal City, nine thousand li', and the fourth, pointing east, a single word: 'Onward.' No distance. A cord tied at the foot of the mast carries a string of knots, and Xiaojiang feels along them one by one. 'Grandpa's knots. He's saying the road east can't be measured.'

name: 山脚木市
Hillfoot Timber Market
before: 山脚下一片空场，堆着一垛垛木料：船板、桅杆、舵杆、肋骨，全是好木头，归墟的漂客盖屋、修船都靠这里。可如今木垛顶上站着一队亡骑，马蹄踩着木料，谁来扛木头就把谁撞下去。木匠们蹲在场边，手里攥着斧子，干看着。

An open yard at the foot of the hills is stacked with timber: ship's planks, masts, rudder stocks, ribs, all fine wood, and every castaway in the Ruins builds houses and mends boats from it. But now a troop of dead riders stands on top of the stacks, hooves on the timber, and rams off anyone who comes to shoulder a beam. The carpenters squat at the edge of the yard, axes in hand, and just watch.
after: 亡骑退了，木匠们一拥而上。领头的老木匠一眼认出了后千里：「泉州码头，龙母摊！那天你们赶跑了刀手，我们这帮扛包的才吃上一碗面线糊。」后来他上了一条贩木船，上个月撞进礁圈，漂到了归墟。他一招呼，满场的木匠都认了你们，木料换金子的买卖开了张。木料上都烙着「千里·二」到「千里·五」：「船是他们自己拆的，拆了给我们盖屋。烧的那条，是另一回事。」

The riders withdraw and the carpenters surge in. Their leader, an old carpenter, recognises Houqianli at once. 'Quanzhou docks, Mother Long's stall! The day you chased off those thugs, us porters finally got a bowl of noodle soup.' Later he signed on with a timber boat, which ran into the reef ring last month and drifted into the Ruins. At his shout every carpenter in the yard takes your side, and timber-for-gold trade opens. All the wood is branded Qianli Two to Qianli Five. 'They took the ships apart themselves and gave us the timber for houses. The one that burned, that's another story.'

name: 缆绳巷
Rope Walk Lane
before: 野地里一条长长的巷子，两边立着木架，架上拉着一根根缆绳，从巷头拉到巷尾，有的粗过人腿。这是从前打缆的地方。一队亡弓占着巷子，把缆绳一根根割断，断一根，巷子里就嘣的一声响，震得架子直晃。

A long lane runs through the open land, wooden frames on either side strung with ropes from end to end, some thicker than a man's leg. It was once a rope walk. A squad of dead archers has taken it and is cutting the ropes one by one, and every time one parts, the lane rings with a twang that sets the frames shaking.
after: 亡弓被赶走了。断口是割的，割得整齐，可缆绳是新打的，结是小桨爷爷的结。漂客们说，这几年守墟人天天来割，割完了，夜里不知谁又给接上，接了割，割了接。小桨把一根断缆接上，打了个结，跟原来那个一模一样：「爷爷教的第一个结，叫『等着』。」

The archers are driven off. The cuts are clean, but the ropes are newly laid, and the knots are Xiaojiang's grandfather's. These past years the keepers have come every day to cut them, the castaways say, and every night someone splices them again: spliced and cut, cut and spliced. Xiaojiang joins a severed rope and ties it off with a knot exactly like the old one. 'The first knot Grandpa ever taught me. It's called Wait.'

name: 覆舟营
Upturned Hull Camp
before: 北屿的高处扣着一条大船的船底，船底朝天，像一座黑色的长屋。三路守墟人以它为营：亡兵在船底下歇着，亡弓趴在龙骨上，亡骑在屿上来回巡。整座北屿上的漂客，夜里都不敢往这边看，说那条船里住着「守墟人的头儿」。

On the high ground of the North Islet lies a great ship's hull, keel to the sky, like a long black hall. Ruin-keepers in three columns have made it their camp: soldiers resting beneath it, archers lying along the keel, riders patrolling the islet. No castaway on the North Islet dares look this way at night. The keepers' chief lives in that ship, they say.
after: 守墟人退进了海里，船底下没有什么头儿，只有一排排睡铺，铺板上刻着一道道「正」字。船底的木料是「千里·五」。舱壁上用炭写着一行大字，墨迹被海雾洇过：「船不烧，不沉，留给后来的人。」底下另有一行歪字，像是有人反驳：「留也没用，东边去不了船。」

The keepers withdraw into the sea. There is no chief beneath the hull, only row on row of bunks, tally marks scratched into every plank. The timber is Qianli Five. On the bulkhead, in charcoal blurred by sea damp, is a line in large characters: 'Do not burn the ships. Do not sink them. Leave them for those who come after.' Below it, in a crooked hand, as if someone were arguing back: 'No use leaving them. Ships can't go east.'

name: 听海石
Listening Stone
before: 北屿东头一块大石，石面上被人坐出了一个窝，窝边凿着一个耳朵形的小坑，贴耳朵正好。一队亡兵占着石头，把漂客赶得远远的，自己却也不坐，只围着站。小桨一上屿就往石头那边跑，被亡兵一枪杆横在胸前。

A great rock at the eastern end of the North Islet has a hollow worn into it by someone's sitting, and beside the hollow is chiselled a little ear-shaped pit, just right for pressing your ear to. A squad of dead soldiers holds the rock and keeps the castaways well away, though they don't sit on it either, only stand around it. The moment Xiaojiang reaches the islet he runs for the rock, and a spear shaft comes across his chest.
after: 亡兵退了，小桨坐进那个窝，把耳朵贴进小坑，听了很久：「底下有声音，很低，像牛在地底下叫。」岛上的老人说，鲍老针当年天天坐这儿听，有一天他忽然跳起来，满岛地喊：「上山！都上山！」大伙跑上了山，那天下午，海就扑上来了。

The soldiers withdraw and Xiaojiang sits in the hollow, presses his ear into the pit and listens a long time. 'There's a sound down there. Very low, like an ox lowing under the ground.' Bao Laozhen sat here every day in those years, the old islanders say, listening. One day he leapt up and ran across the whole island shouting, 'Up the mountain! Everyone up the mountain!' They all ran uphill, and that afternoon the sea came pouncing ashore.

name: 碎木湾
Driftwood Bay
before: 海边一道湾，湾里漂着一层碎木头，船板、桶板、舱门，挤得看不见水。一队亡弓守着湾口，见有漂客划小船进来捞木头，就射船底。漂客们说，这湾里的木头都是那年大浪打碎的东西，十年了还没漂干净，静水里，什么都漂不走。

A bay on the coast is carpeted with broken wood, planks, barrel staves, hatch covers, packed so tight you can't see the water. A squad of dead archers holds the mouth and shoots the hull of any castaway boat that paddles in to gather wood. Everything in this bay was smashed by the great wave that year, the castaways say. Ten years and it still hasn't drifted away; in still water, nothing ever drifts away.
after: 亡弓被赶走，漂客们划着小船进湾捞木头。龚墨斗捞起一块舱门，门上烧焦了一半，另一半刻着「千里·三」。原来那条烧过的船不是火烧的：大浪打碎了岸上的灶屋，炭火扣在了船上。他松了口气：「不是人烧的。」

The archers are driven off and the castaways paddle in to gather wood. Gong Modou fishes out a hatch cover, half charred, the other half carved 'Qianli Three'. So the burned ship was never set alight: the great wave smashed the cookhouse ashore and tipped its live coals onto the ship. He lets out a breath. 'Nobody burned it.'

name: 避浪坪
Wave Refuge Terrace
before: 山脚上一片平坪，坪上搭着几十间矮棚，是那年大浪时漂客们逃上来住的，浪退了，有人就再没下山。一队亡骑这几天天天往坪上冲，拿枪杆把棚子一间间挑翻，像是要把人往山下赶。坪上的老人们不肯走：「下面淹过一回，上面不会淹。」

A level terrace on the lower slopes is crowded with dozens of low shelters, built by castaways who fled up here the year of the great wave; when the water went down, some never came back down. For days a troop of dead riders has charged onto the terrace, flipping shelters over with their spear shafts as though trying to drive the people downhill. The old folk refuse to budge. 'Down there it flooded once. Up here it won't.'
after: 亡骑退了。坪边立着一根木杆，杆上刻着那天浪到的高度，比坪沿低了一人多。杆下压着一块木牌，是鲍老针的字：「海先退了半里，鱼都蹦在滩上，那就是浪要来了，不许去捡鱼，往高处跑。」老人们说，那天正是这块牌子救了一岛人，捡鱼的孩子全被拽了回来。

The riders withdraw. A wooden post at the terrace's edge is marked with the height the wave reached that day, a man's height and more below the terrace rim. Pinned beneath it is a board in Bao Laozhen's hand: 'If the sea pulls back half a li and the fish are flapping on the sand, the wave is coming. Do not go after the fish. Run for high ground.' That board saved the whole island that day, the old folk say. Every child who ran out for the fish was dragged back.

name: 三老说
Three Elders' Tale
before: 大路边一棵大榕树下，三个漂客老人天天坐着吵架，吵的是同一件事：千里号的船是怎么没的。今天吵得最凶，一队亡兵站在树下，围着他们，像是也在听。三个老人谁也不理守墟人，各拍各的大腿：「我亲眼看见的！」

Under a great banyan beside the main road three castaway elders sit and argue every day, always about the same thing: how the Qianli's ships came to be gone. Today the row is at its worst. A squad of dead soldiers stands round them under the tree as if listening too. None of the three pays the keepers any mind; each slaps his own thigh. 'I saw it with my own eyes!'
after: 亡兵退了，三个老人一人一个说法。头一个说：船主下令烧了船，断了回头路。第二个说：守墟人一夜劈了船，不让活人走。第三个说：是大浪打碎的，跟谁都没关系。三个人说完，互相瞪着，又一齐看你们：「你们说，谁对？」龚墨斗摸着下巴：「都看见了一点，都没看全。」

The soldiers withdraw and the three elders each give their version. The first: the ship's master ordered the ships burned to cut off any way back. The second: the keepers split the ships in a single night so the living couldn't leave. The third: the great wave smashed them, nobody's fault at all. Having spoken, they glare at one another, then all turn to you. 'Well, which of us is right?' Gong Modou rubs his chin. 'Each of you saw a piece. None of you saw the whole.'

name: 北屿鸡寮
North Islet Coop
before: 北屿背阴的一面，一排鸡寮靠着崖壁，寮里是船头屋阿婆的鸡生下的一大群鸡，满屿乱跑。一队亡弓占着鸡寮，把鸡蛋一窝窝扔进海里，鸡赶出来又不吃，就那么扔着。阿婆的孙女蹲在寮外，拿裙子兜着最后几个蛋，抽抽搭搭。

On the shady side of the North Islet a row of coops backs onto the cliff, home to the countless descendants of the prow-house granny's chickens, which run all over the islet. A squad of dead archers has taken the coops and is throwing the eggs into the sea nest by nest. They drive the hens out too, not to eat, just to throw. The granny's granddaughter squats outside, cradling the last few eggs in her skirt and sniffling.
after: 亡弓被赶走，鸡又回了寮。阿婆的孙女说，这群鸡的老祖宗是千里号上带下来的，船上的人说「船上要有鸡，替人数日子」，下船的时候把鸡留给了阿婆。龚墨斗想起了雾海镇雾号上那只芦花鸡：「镇雾号上那只，跟这一窝是一个脾气。」

The archers are driven off and the hens go back in. The granddaughter says the first of this flock came off the Qianli. 'A ship needs a hen to count the days,' the sailors said, and when they came ashore they left the hens with Granny. Gong Modou remembers the speckled rooster aboard the Zhenwu in the Sea of Fog. 'Same temper as that one.'
first: 鸡寮背后抄出亡弓扔剩下的六篮鸡蛋、一窝刚出壳的小鸡，还有守墟人不知从哪儿拖来的十几捆干海草，码得整整齐齐，像要给谁铺床。

Behind the coops you find six baskets of eggs the archers didn't get to, a brood of newly hatched chicks, and a dozen bales of dried seaweed the keepers dragged from who knows where, stacked neatly as if to make someone a bed.
pass: 每次路过，阿婆的孙女都兜着一裙子鸡蛋跑下崖来，挑最大的给你们：「奶奶说，给数日子的人，吃数日子的鸡下的蛋。」

Each time you pass, the granny's granddaughter comes running down the cliff with a skirt full of eggs and picks out the biggest for you. 'Granny says people who count the days should eat eggs from the hens that count them.'

name: 舵杆滩
Rudder Stock Strand
before: 海边沙滩上竖着一根粗大的舵杆，铁力木的，黑得发亮，半截埋进沙里，另半截比人还高。一队亡骑绕着舵杆跑，谁要拔它，就被马撞开。龚墨斗一看就直了眼，扔下烟袋冲了上去：「铁力木！这一根，十年不烂！」

A massive rudder stock stands upright on the beach, ironwood, gleaming black, half buried in the sand and the other half taller than a man. A troop of dead riders gallops round it and bowls over anyone who tries to pull it up. Gong Modou's eyes go wide at the sight; he drops his pipe and charges in. 'Ironwood! A stock like that won't rot in ten years!'
after: 亡骑退了，龚墨斗抱着舵杆摩挲了半天，杆上刻着「千里·二」。他说造船的规矩，拆船不拆舵：「舵是船的命，拆了舵，船就真死了。」可这根舵却是被好好地卸下来，竖在这儿的，像插一根桩，像在说：船不走了，可要记着，它是能走的。

The riders withdraw and Gong Modou runs his hands over the stock for a long while. It is carved 'Qianli Two'. Shipwrights have a rule, he says: break up a ship, but never break its rudder. 'The rudder is a ship's life. Take the rudder apart and the ship's truly dead.' Yet this one was carefully unshipped and stood here like a post, as if to say: the ship is going no further, but remember, it could have.

name: 锯木岭
Sawpit Ridge
before: 山脚下一道土岭，岭上挖着几个长坑，坑上横着木头，是锯木头用的锯坑，一人站在上头，一人站在坑底，一推一拉。一队亡兵蹲在坑里，一个上一个下，学着锯木头的样子，手里却什么都没有，一推一拉，一推一拉，锯了不知多少年。

On an earth ridge at the foot of the hills are dug long pits with logs laid across them: sawpits, one man standing above and one below, push and pull. A squad of dead soldiers crouches in them, one above, one below, miming the sawing with nothing in their hands, push and pull, push and pull, for who knows how many years.
after: 亡兵退了，坑底还堆着厚厚的锯末，翻开来，底下压着一把大锯，锯条上刻着「千里号·木作」。龚墨斗拿锯齿比了比北屿船头的断口：就是这一把。「是锯的，」他说，「一个人在上，一个人在下，锯了好些天。守墟人在旁边看着，看会了。」

The soldiers withdraw. The pit floors are deep in sawdust, and beneath it lies a great saw, its blade stamped 'Qianli. Carpentry'. Gong Modou holds its teeth against the cut he saw on the North Islet prow: this is the one. 'Sawn,' he says. 'One man above, one below, for days on end. The keepers stood by and watched, and learned it.'

name: 钉子铺
Nail Smithy
before: 野地里一间打铁铺，炉子冷着，铁砧上摆着一排船钉，有长有短，一律掰直了。一队亡弓守着铺子，铺里的铁匠是个漂客，被他们逼着把钉子一根根掰弯，掰弯了，他们又拿去掰直，掰直了，再递给他。铁匠的手上全是血泡。

A smithy stands in the open, its forge cold, a row of ship's nails laid on the anvil, long and short, every one hammered straight. A squad of dead archers holds the shop, and the smith, a castaway, is made to bend the nails one by one. Once bent, the archers take them and straighten them, then hand them back to him. The smith's palms are covered in blood blisters.
after: 亡弓退了，铁匠瘫在砧子边。他说这些钉子是千里号拆船拆下来的，那几年他天天替他们掰直，好让漂客们盖屋用，一根一根，掰了上万根。「守墟人看了几年，学会了掰直，」他搓着手，「可它们不知道钉子拿来干什么。」

The archers withdraw and the smith slumps against his anvil. These are nails from the Qianli's ships, he says. In those years he straightened them every day so the castaways could build houses with them, one by one, tens of thousands. 'The keepers watched for years and learned to straighten them,' he says, rubbing his hands. 'But they never learned what nails are for.'

name: 旗杆坊
Flagpole Lane
before: 大路边一条小街，街口立着一根旗杆，杆头没有旗，挂着一只空了的鸟笼。街两边的屋子都是船板盖的，门是舱门，窗是舷窗。一队亡兵在街上来回走，挨家挨户把舷窗一扇扇关上，漂客们开一扇，它们关一扇。

A narrow street off the main road, a flagpole at its mouth with no flag, only an empty birdcage hanging from the top. Every house along it is built of ship's planking, with hatch covers for doors and portholes for windows. A squad of dead soldiers paces the street closing the portholes one by one, house by house; the castaways open one, the keepers close it.
after: 亡兵退了，舷窗一扇扇打开。整条街就是四条船：门牌上写着「千里·二」「千里·三」……街尾一座小屋，门楣上写着「领港寮」，屋里一张空铺，铺头一只竹筒，筒口塞着蜡。小桨拿着竹筒没拆，手一直在抖：「是爷爷的。」

The soldiers withdraw and the portholes open one by one. The whole street is four ships: the door plates read 'Qianli Two', 'Qianli Three'... At the end stands a little house with 'Pilots' Lodge' over the door, an empty bunk inside, and at its head a bamboo tube stoppered with wax. Xiaojiang holds the tube without opening it, his hands shaking. 'It's Grandpa's.'

name: 拆船簿
Breaking Ledger
before: 野地里一座小木屋，屋门钉死了，门上贴着一张发黄的告示，盖着千里号的船印。一队亡骑守在屋外，绕着屋子转，谁要撕告示，它们就冲过来。漂客们说屋里锁着一本簿子，十年了没人见过，见过的人都说里头记的是「船是怎么没的」。

A little wooden hut in the open, its door nailed shut and a yellowed notice pasted on it bearing the Qianli's seal. A troop of dead riders circles outside and charges anyone who tries to tear the notice down. A book is locked inside, the castaways say. No one has seen it in ten years, but those who once did say it records 'how the ships came to be gone'.
after: 亡骑散了，你们撬开门，簿子摆在桌上。头一页是许潮生的字：「船主在蜃楼未至，领港代令：拆二、三、四、五号，木料分与漂客，钉、缆、帆尽留。一号不拆，候船主。」最后一页只有半句：「三号舱失火，大浪……」后面撕掉了，撕口还新，往山那边去的路上，有马蹄印。

The riders scatter, you prise the door open, and the book lies on the table. The first page is in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'The master stays in the Mirage and has not come. By the pilot's order in her stead: break up Two, Three, Four and Five. Timber to be shared among the castaways; nails, cables and sails all left here. Number One not to be broken; she waits for her master.' The last page holds only half a sentence: 'Fire in Three's hold, the great wave...' The rest is torn out, the tear still fresh, and on the road towards the hills there are hoofprints.

name: 二号货舱
Hold Number Two
before: 海边一座半埋在沙里的大货舱，是「千里·二」拆剩下的底舱，舱口盖着油布。看舱的是个独眼老水手，自称当年留下看货的，十年来谁来要货，他都要先问一句「拿什么换」。可这几天一队亡弓守在舱口，连他自己都进不去，他坐在沙堆上骂：「我的舱！我看了十年！」

A great cargo hold half buried in the sand on the coast: the lower hold of Qianli Two, all that was left when she was broken up, its hatch covered with oilcloth. Its keeper is a one-eyed old sailor who says he stayed behind to mind the goods, and for ten years he has asked anyone who wants cargo, 'What will you trade for it?' For days now a squad of dead archers has held the hatch, and even he can't get in. He sits on a sand heap cursing. 'My hold! Ten years I've minded it!'
after: 亡弓被赶走，独眼老水手爬回舱里，掀开油布：一捆捆十年前的货，瓷器、铜锣、成箱的针。他眯着独眼打量你们，佩服你们的身手，肯拿十年前的货换你们的新货。「船主说了，货不能白给，得换，」他说，「换着换着，路就通了。」

The archers are driven off and the one-eyed sailor climbs back into his hold and pulls back the oilcloth: bale after bale of ten-year-old cargo, porcelain, brass gongs, crates of needles. He sizes you up with his one eye, impressed by how you fight, and agrees to trade his decade-old goods for your new ones. 'The master said cargo's not to be given away, it's to be traded,' he says. 'Keep trading and the road stays open.'

name: 半山汲站
Hillside Water Stop
before: 半山腰一处泉眼，泉边一座石屋，是大浪那年漂客们逃上山时喝水的地方。如今一伙落难海盗占了泉眼，在屋里囤水卖水，一瓢一钱，山下的漂客挑不起这个价，只好喝咸水，喝得满嘴起泡。守泉的海盗弓手站在石屋顶上，谁靠近就放箭。

A spring halfway up the hillside with a stone hut beside it, where the castaways drank when they fled uphill the year of the great wave. Now a band of shipwrecked pirates has seized it, hoarding water in the hut and selling it at a copper a ladle. The castaways below can't afford it and drink brackish water until their mouths blister. The pirates' archers stand on the hut roof and shoot anyone who comes near.
after: 海盗被赶下了山，泉水又顺着竹管流到了山下。石屋墙上刻着一行字：「浪退后第三日，鲍老针寻得此泉。」漂客们说，那年要不是老针听出了这口泉在石头底下响，山上的人要渴死一半。

The pirates are driven down the hill and the spring water runs down to the lowlands through bamboo pipes again. A line is carved on the hut wall: 'Third day after the wave receded. Bao Laozhen found this spring.' If Old Needle hadn't heard this spring gurgling under the rock that year, say the castaways, half the people on the mountain would have died of thirst.
first: 石屋里抄出海盗囤的二十缸泉水、一筐椰子、一捆弓箭，还有一本卖水的账，一瓢一钱，记了整整三年，最大的一笔是「卖给山下老阿婆，一瓢，赊」。

In the hut you seize the pirates' hoard: twenty vats of spring water, a basket of coconuts, a bundle of bows and arrows, and their water-selling ledger, a copper a ladle, kept for three full years. The largest entry: 'Sold to the old woman below, one ladle, on credit.'
pass: 每次路过，山上的漂客都替你们把水囊灌满，再折一根竹管给你们：「老针说过，水往低处走，人往高处走，竹管带着，哪儿都能接上水。」

Each time you pass, the hill folk fill your water skins and cut you a length of bamboo pipe. 'Old Needle used to say, water runs downhill and people climb up. Carry a pipe and you can tap water anywhere.'

name: 一号空泊
Empty Berth One
before: 大路尽头一道小河汊，汊口一座石砌的码头，码头上刻着一个大大的「一」字，泊位却是空的，系船柱磨得发亮。一队亡兵守在码头上，排成一排，像在等船靠岸。漂客们说，那年大浪退了以后，这个泊位就空了，一号船不见了，没人知道去了哪儿。

The main road ends at a little creek where a stone quay is carved with a great character 'One'. The berth is empty, its bollard worn shiny. A squad of dead soldiers stands on the quay in a row as though waiting for a ship to come in. After the great wave went back that year, the castaways say, this berth was empty. Ship Number One was gone, and no one knows where.
after: 亡兵退了。阿舟摸着系船柱上那道绳痕，笑了一下：「我哥在泉州也给我留了一号泊。」龚墨斗量了量河汊的水深，又抬头看了看东边的野地，喃喃道：「这么大的浪，船不在海里，会在哪儿……」小桨把爷爷的竹筒贴在耳朵上，像在听什么。

The soldiers withdraw. Azhou runs a hand over the rope groove in the bollard and smiles slightly. 'My brother kept Berth One for me back in Quanzhou too.' Gong Modou sounds the creek's depth, then looks up at the open country to the east, muttering, 'A wave that big. If the ship's not in the sea, where would it be...' Xiaojiang holds his grandfather's bamboo tube to his ear as if listening for something.
